newsitem.title: UK: GEC, SIEMENS RUMOURS FUEL DEAL HOPES.
newsitem.headline: GEC, SIEMENS RUMOURS FUEL DEAL HOPES.

text.p: Fresh speculation that General Electric Co Plc and Siemens AG are close to clinching deals with each other in telecoms and defence, have fuelled hopes of GEC moving quickly to deliver shareholder value, said analysts on Monday.

A Sunday Times report said GEC was close to agreeing to sell its 60 percent stake in the GPT telecoms joint venture to partner Siemens and was the leading bid to buy the German group's defence arm Siemens Plessey, which is also up for sale.
Both companies refused to comment about the rumours.

But, analysts were positive. "I think there has to be every probability of this happening," said James Heal, analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. He also believed GEC was front-runner in the race for Siemens Plessey.
The rumours come a month after GEC managing director George Simpson unveiled his strategic blueprint to take the group forward.
A spokesman for Siemens in London said of the GPT stake story, "Speculation has been rife on these issues for some time."
However, Siemens has said in the past it was happy with the performance of telecoms and would like to grow that business.
On the GPT venture, GEC said last month it had considered divestment but backed away from a sale as the two sides could not agree on price.
The Sunday Times report said the two sides' evaluations of GEC's 60 percent stake had since converged.
Analysts estimated GEC valued its stake at one billion stg. The gap between GEC's and Siemens' value was believed to be around 100 million stg.

Rumours of speedy restructuring were likely fuelled by appointment last week of John Mayo as finance director. The move was welcomed, helping push GEC's shares up 50 pence, with Mayo seen as a deal-maker by the market.
GEC's shares were easier on Monday at 394p, down 4-1/2 pence, after last week's powerful surge.
Mayo will join GEC from Zeneca Group Plc, where he was a key figure in its demerger from former parent Imperial Chemical Industries Plc .
One dealer said the market had "put two and two together" in the hope that Mayo would assist Simpson in getting GEC moving on its restructuring.
